chunks: From him, from Usman ibn Isa, from Muyassar, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

key_terms.غَبْنٌ: Cheating, deception, or defrauding in trade

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on cheating a believer in business transactions according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to define 'ghabn' (deception or unfair advantage) as inherently prohibited in commercial transactions. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on moral integrity in trade, extending beyond mere legal validity to include spiritual purity and justice between believers. It serves as a foundational principle for Islamic commercial ethics, ensuring that transactions are not only contractually sound but also ethically fair.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Usman Bin Isa, from Muyassar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
en.sarwar: 15. It is narrated from the narrator of previous Hadith from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Muyassir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Selling above fair piece to a believing person is unlawful.’”
